label: Basic
description: Basic code block. Best for a static TypeScript snippet with line numbers, the resolved language label and a header copy button.

label: Pinned Copy
description: Pinned copy button. Best for a headerless snippet whose copy button floats over the code's corner.

label: Streaming Agent
description: Streaming agent response. Best for a route handler typed out 3 characters per tick under a Generating badge, then Done, with a Replay.

label: AI Chat
description: AI chat with code. Best for a 2 turn transcript with avatars, where the reply mixes text and a code block.

label: Diff Summary
description: Diff with change summary. Best for removed and added lines of a single file marked by number, with the change summed up in header badges.

label: Transformer Diff
description: Diff from line marks. Best for lines 2 and 3 marked removed and line 5 added by the caller (the web uses a Shiki transformer).

label: Highlights
description: Highlighted lines and words. Best for a connection config with lines 2 to 4 tinted and two words marked wherever they appear.

label: Focus Walkthrough
description: Focus walkthrough. Best for a 3 step tour of a checkout function, chosen with segments in the header, the step's lines in focus and the rest dimmed.

label: Terminal Output
description: Terminal output. Best for build output as plain text under a Terminal header, with nothing to colour.

label: Long File
description: Long file with expand. Best for a generated file excerpt numbered from 120 and held to 8 lines until opened.

label: Diagnostics & Actions
description: Diagnostics. Best for a function with an error line and a warning line, each with a note under it, tallied in header badges, with copy.

label: Line Selection
description: Line selection. Best for tapping line numbers to pick lines, a badge counting them, and asking about the pick.

label: Search In File
description: Search in file. Best for a header search field that marks each match as you type, a badge counting them, and a match-case switch.

label: File Tabs
description: File tabs in a dense frame. Best for snippets in TSX, Python, SQL and Bash behind segments in a dense Frame.

label: Pre-Highlighted Lines
description: Pre-coloured lines. Best for hand-built tokens that colour 4 Python keywords, passed as lines.

label: Before & After
description: Before and after. Best for a loop refactored into a reduce, as 2 blocks with Before and After headers.

label: Soft Wrap
description: Soft wrap. Best for a single-line policy that starts wrapped, with a switch and a badge saying which way it is.

label: Unified Patch
description: Unified patch review. Best for a 2 file patch, one block per file, each with its added and removed counts.

label: Design Token Theme
description: Palette in tone colours. Best for palette tokens drawn in the theme's tone colours (the phone's code colours follow the app theme).

label: Always Dark
description: Hero block. Best for a snippet behind 3 window dots with a highlighted line and a marked word (the phone follows the app's theme, with no forced-dark scope).

label: Dark Terminal
description: Test log. Best for a log built token by token: passes in green, a failure in red, timings dimmed.

label: Accept & Reject
description: Accept and reject. Best for an agent fix in a Card, with Reject and Accept in the block's footer.

label: Code Folding
description: Nested code folding. Best for a sync function with 5 regions that fold from their first line's number, the inner branch folded at first.

label: Fix With AI
description: Fix with AI. Best for a reduce missing its initial value flagged on line 3, with a gutter button that asks for a fix and applies it.

label: Reference Lines
description: Reference lines in chat. Best for a gutter + that adds a line to the message as a chip.

label: External Scroll
description: Scrolled by its card. Best for a Card with 3 changed files that size to their content, scrolled together inside a fixed height.

label: ANSI Terminal
description: ANSI terminal output. Best for test output with raw colour escapes turned into coloured tokens by ansiToCodeLines.
